section_1.title: The Big Picture: Static vs. Dynamic
section_1.content: Introduction to the core philosophy of calculus. Contrast the world of algebra (static shapes and constant speeds) with the real world (curvy shapes and changing speeds). Use the 'Flash' vs. 'The Turtle' analogy to show the need for measuring change at a specific moment.
section_1.example: A car speeding up on a highway. Algebra tells you the average speed over an hour, but Calculus tells you the exact speed at the moment you pass a speed camera.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Power of Approximation
section_2.content: Introduce the concept of 'Limits' and the 'Infinitesimal.' Explain how complex problems can be solved by breaking them into infinitely small, simpler pieces. This sets the stage for both derivatives and integrals.
section_2.example: Archimedes approximating a circle by fitting a polygon inside it. As the number of sides (n) approaches infinity, the polygon becomes the circle.

section_3.title: Differentiation: Zooming In for Truth
section_3.content: Focus on the 'Derivative.' Visually demonstrate that if you zoom in enough on any smooth curve, it eventually looks like a straight line. This 'straight line' is the tangent, representing the instantaneous rate of change.
section_3.example: A roller coaster track. At any single point on a steep drop, your 'direction' is a straight arrow (the derivative). We calculate this by making the distance between two points on the track infinitely small.

section_4.title: Integration: Summing the Infinite
section_4.content: Focus on the 'Integral.' Explain it as the reverse of slicing. If differentiation breaks things down, integration glues them back together to find the 'Total.' Represent this graphically as the area under a curve.
section_4.example: Calculating the total amount of water in a leaking bucket. If you know the 'rate' of the leak at every second (the derivative), integration sums those infinite tiny drips to tell you the total volume lost.

section_5.title: The Fundamental Theorem: The Great Bridge
section_5.content: Reveal the 'Secret' of calculus: Differentiation and Integration are inverse operations. This is the bridge that connects the slope of a graph to the area underneath it. Use a 'Mountain Climber' visual to explain the link between height and steepness.
section_5.example: A 'Growth Machine': If the machine tracks how fast a tree grows (Derivative), the total height of the tree (Integral) is simply the accumulation of that growth. One undoes the other.

section_6.title: Calculus in Action: The Modern World
section_6.content: Summarize how these two concepts allow us to model everything in motion. From planetary orbits to the spread of a virus, calculus is the 'engine' under the hood of physics and engineering.
section_6.example: A SpaceX Falcon 9 landing. Calculus is used to constantly calculate the changing fuel weight and air resistance to adjust the engines at every millisecond for a perfect touchdown.

section_1.title: The Big Picture: Static vs. Dynamic
section_1.content: Introduction to the core philosophy of calculus. Contrast the world of algebra (static shapes and constant speeds) with the real world (curvy shapes and changing speeds). Use the 'Flash' vs. 'The Turtle' analogy to show the need for measuring change at a specific moment.
section_1.example: A car speeding up on a highway. Algebra tells you the average speed over an hour, but Calculus tells you the exact speed at the moment you pass a speed camera.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Power of Approximation
section_2.content: Introduce the concept of 'Limits' and the 'Infinitesimal.' Explain how complex problems can be solved by breaking them into infinitely small, simpler pieces. This sets the stage for both derivatives and integrals.
section_2.example: Archimedes approximating a circle by fitting a polygon inside it. As the number of sides (n) approaches infinity, the polygon becomes the circle.

section_3.title: Differentiation: Zooming In for Truth
section_3.content: Focus on the 'Derivative.' Visually demonstrate that if you zoom in enough on any smooth curve, it eventually looks like a straight line. This 'straight line' is the tangent, representing the instantaneous rate of change.
section_3.example: A roller coaster track. At any single point on a steep drop, your 'direction' is a straight arrow (the derivative). We calculate this by making the distance between two points on the track infinitely small.

section_4.title: Integration: Summing the Infinite
section_4.content: Focus on the 'Integral.' Explain it as the reverse of slicing. If differentiation breaks things down, integration glues them back together to find the 'Total.' Represent this graphically as the area under a curve.
section_4.example: Calculating the total amount of water in a leaking bucket. If you know the 'rate' of the leak at every second (the derivative), integration sums those infinite tiny drips to tell you the total volume lost.

section_5.title: The Fundamental Theorem: The Great Bridge
section_5.content: Reveal the 'Secret' of calculus: Differentiation and Integration are inverse operations. This is the bridge that connects the slope of a graph to the area underneath it. Use a 'Mountain Climber' visual to explain the link between height and steepness.
section_5.example: A 'Growth Machine': If the machine tracks how fast a tree grows (Derivative), the total height of the tree (Integral) is simply the accumulation of that growth. One undoes the other.

section_6.title: Calculus in Action: The Modern World
section_6.content: Summarize how these two concepts allow us to model everything in motion. From planetary orbits to the spread of a virus, calculus is the 'engine' under the hood of physics and engineering.
section_6.example: A SpaceX Falcon 9 landing. Calculus is used to constantly calculate the changing fuel weight and air resistance to adjust the engines at every millisecond for a perfect touchdown.

section_1.title: The Big Picture: Static vs. Dynamic
lecture_lines: Algebra handles static shapes and constant speeds perfectly.
But the real world is curvy and constantly changing.
Calculus measures change at a specific, exact moment.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Power of Approximation
lecture_lines: Complex shapes are hard to measure directly.
We can approximate them using many simpler pieces.
As pieces become infinitely small, the approximation becomes exact.

section_3.title: Differentiation: Zooming In for Truth
lecture_lines: Zooming into any smooth curve eventually reveals a line.
This straight line represents the instantaneous rate of change.
On a roller coaster, your direction is a tangent.
We find this by narrowing the gap between points.
This process of finding slopes is called differentiation.

Display text 'Differentiation' in #FF8C00 and flash it. Change lecture line 5 color to #FFFF00.

section_4.title: Integration: Summing the Infinite
lecture_lines: Integration glues tiny, infinite pieces back into a whole.
It calculates the total accumulation over a period.
Visually, this is the area under a curve.
If we sum every tiny drip from a bucket...
We find the total volume of water lost.

section_5.title: The Fundamental Theorem: The Great Bridge
lecture_lines: Differentiation and integration are actually perfect opposites.
One finds the slope, the other finds the area.
A climber’s steepness at any point determines their height.
Tracking growth rate reveals the total growth achieved.
This bridge connects the rate of change to accumulation.

outline.title: The Fundamental Theorem: The Great Bridge
outline.content: Reveal the 'Secret' of calculus: Differentiation and Integration are inverse operations. This is the bridge that connects the slope of a graph to the area underneath it. Use a 'Mountain Climber' visual to explain the link between height and steepness.
outline.example: A 'Growth Machine': If the machine tracks how fast a tree grows (Derivative), the total height of the tree (Integral) is simply the accumulation of that growth. One undoes the other.

outline.title: Differentiation: Zooming In for Truth
outline.content: Focus on the 'Derivative.' Visually demonstrate that if you zoom in enough on any smooth curve, it eventually looks like a straight line. This 'straight line' is the tangent, representing the instantaneous rate of change.
outline.example: A roller coaster track. At any single point on a steep drop, your 'direction' is a straight arrow (the derivative). We calculate this by making the distance between two points on the track infinitely small.

outline.title: Prerequisite: The Power of Approximation
outline.content: Introduce the concept of 'Limits' and the 'Infinitesimal.' Explain how complex problems can be solved by breaking them into infinitely small, simpler pieces. This sets the stage for both derivatives and integrals.
outline.example: Archimedes approximating a circle by fitting a polygon inside it. As the number of sides (n) approaches infinity, the polygon becomes the circle.

outline.content: Introduction to the core philosophy of calculus. Contrast the world of algebra (static shapes and constant speeds) with the real world (curvy shapes and changing speeds). Use the 'Flash' vs. 'The Turtle' analogy to show the need for measuring change at a specific moment.
outline.example: A car speeding up on a highway. Algebra tells you the average speed over an hour, but Calculus tells you the exact speed at the moment you pass a speed camera.

outline.title: Integration: Summing the Infinite
outline.content: Focus on the 'Integral.' Explain it as the reverse of slicing. If differentiation breaks things down, integration glues them back together to find the 'Total.' Represent this graphically as the area under a curve.
outline.example: Calculating the total amount of water in a leaking bucket. If you know the 'rate' of the leak at every second (the derivative), integration sums those infinite tiny drips to tell you the total volume lost.

It calculates the total accumulation over a period.
Visually, this is the area under a curve.
If we sum every tiny drip from a bucket...
We find the total volume of water lost.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        # The right side occupies roughly x in [0, 6]
        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Adjusting center of the grid system to the right side
                x = 1.0 + j * 1.0
                y = 2.5 - i * 1.0
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title_str = "The Fundamental Theorem: The Great Bridge"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Differentiation and integration are actually perfect opposites.",
            "One finds the slope, the other finds the area.",
            "A climber’s steepness at any point determines their height.",

        self.setup_layout(title_str, lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Split screen: Left side shows a derivative graph, right shows an integral graph.
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # Derivative Graph: f(x) = 2x
        deriv_axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 3], y_range=[0, 6], axis_config={"include_tip": False}, x_length=2.5, y_length=2.5)
        deriv_graph = deriv_axes.plot(lambda x: 2*x, color=YELLOW)
        deriv_label = Text("Derivative", font_size=16, color=YELLOW)
        deriv_group = VGroup(deriv_axes, deriv_graph, deriv_label).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(deriv_group, "A1", "C3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Integral Graph: F(x) = x^2
        int_axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 3], y_range=[0, 9], axis_config={"include_tip": False}, x_length=2.5, y_length=2.5)
        int_graph = int_axes.plot(lambda x: x**2, color=CYAN)
        int_label = Text("Integral", font_size=16, color=CYAN)
        int_group = VGroup(int_axes, int_graph, int_label).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(int_group, "A4", "F3", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(Create(deriv_group), Create(int_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight the slope on the left (#FFFF00) and the area on the right (#00FFFF).
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # Slope highlight
        p1 = deriv_axes.c2p(1, 2)
        p2 = deriv_axes.c2p(2, 4)
        slope_line = Line(p1, p2, color=YELLOW, stroke_width=6)
        slope_label = Text("Slope", font_size=14, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(slope_label, "B3", scale_factor=0.8)

        # Area highlight
        area = int_axes.get_area(int_graph, x_range=[0, 2], color=CYAN, opacity=0.3)
        area_label = Text("Area", font_size=14, color=CYAN)
        self.place_at_grid(area_label, "B6", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(Create(slope_line), Write(slope_label), FadeIn(area), Write(area_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Show a climber icon (#FF8C00) on a mountain; display steepness arrows.
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        mountain_axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4], y_range=[0, 4], x_length=3, y_length=2)
        mountain_curve = mountain_axes.plot(lambda x: np.sin(x) + 1, color=GREY)
        climber = Triangle(color="#FF8C00", fill_opacity=1).scale(0.1)
        
        # Steepness arrows
        arrow1 = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=UP*0.5, color="#FF8C00").scale(0.5)
        arrow2 = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*0.5+UP*0.3, color="#FF8C00").scale(0.5)
        steepness_group = VGroup(arrow1, arrow2).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5)
        
        mountain_viz = VGroup(mountain_axes, mountain_curve)
        self.place_in_area(mountain_viz, "D1", "F3", scale_factor=0.8) # Adjusted position for better flow
        self.place_at_grid(climber, "E1", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(steepness_group, "F1", scale_factor=1.0)

        # Movement animation
        tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        climber.add_updater(lambda m: m.move_to(mountain_axes.c2p(tracker.get_value(), np.sin(tracker.get_value()) + 1) + UP*0.2))

        self.play(Create(mountain_viz), FadeIn(climber), Create(steepness_group))
        self.play(tracker.animate.set_value(3), run_time=2)
        climber.clear_updaters()
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Show a growing tree icon (#00FF00) whose height matches the integral area.
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        tree_trunk = Rectangle(width=0.2, height=0.5, color="#8B4513", fill_opacity=1)
        tree_foliage = VGroup(
            Triangle(color="#00FF00", fill_opacity=1).scale(0.4),
            Triangle(color="#00FF00", fill_opacity=1).scale(0.4).shift(UP*0.2),
            Triangle(color="#00FF00", fill_opacity=1).scale(0.4).shift(UP*0.4)
        )
        tree = VGroup(tree_trunk, tree_foliage).arrange(UP, buff=0)
        self.place_in_area(tree, "D4", "F6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        growth_tracker = ValueTracker(0.1)
        # Note: Scaling the group might be tricky with center point, but for visual effect it works.
        tree.add_updater(lambda m: m.set(height=growth_tracker.get_value()))

        growth_label = Text("Accumulated Growth", font_size=16, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(growth_label, "D6", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(FadeIn(tree), Write(growth_label))
        self.play(growth_tracker.animate.set_value(2), run_time=2)
        tree.clear_updaters()
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Draw a bridge (#FFFFFF) connecting the concepts of 'Slope' and 'Area'.
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        bridge_base = Line(self.grid["B3"], self.grid["B6"], color=WHITE, stroke_width=4)
        bridge_label = Text("THE BRIDGE", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(bridge_label, "B3", "B6", scale_factor=1.0)
        bridge_label.shift(UP*0.5)

        self.play(Create(bridge_base), Write(bridge_label))
        self.wait(2)

                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from shared state
        title = "Differentiation: Zooming In for Truth"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Zooming into any smooth curve eventually reveals a line.",
            "This straight line represents the instantaneous rate of change.",
            "On a roller coaster, your direction is a tangent.",
            "We find this by narrowing the gap between points.",
            "This process of finding slopes is called differentiation."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # Define a roller coaster curve (cubic for smooth look)
        curve_func = lambda x: 0.1 * x**3 - 0.2 * x
        curve = FunctionGraph(curve_func, x_range=[-3, 3], color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_in_area(curve, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Create(curve))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Zoom effect: Transition to a nearly straight line at x=0
        # Derivative at x=0: f'(0) = 0.3(0)^2 - 0.2 = -0.2
        # We simulate zoom by replacing with a straight segment
        line_start = self.grid["C2"]
        line_end = self.grid["E5"]
        zoomed_line = Line(start=line_start, end=line_end, color="#FFFF00")
        
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(curve, zoomed_line))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        tangent_label = Text("Tangent", font_size=24, color="#FF8C00")
        self.place_at_grid(tangent_label, "B3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(tangent_label))
        self.play(Flash(tangent_label, color="#FF8C00"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # Car icon - small triangle oriented along the line
        angle = np.arctan2(line_end[1] - line_start[1], line_end[0] - line_start[0])
        car = Triangle(color="#FFFF00", fill_opacity=1).scale(0.15)
        car.rotate(angle - PI/2) # Triangle default points UP
        car.move_to(line_start)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(car))
        self.play(car.animate.move_to(line_end), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # Transition back to curve to show points converging
        curve_context = FunctionGraph(curve_func, x_range=[-2.5, 2.5], color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_in_area(curve_context, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(zoomed_line, car, tangent_label),
            FadeIn(curve_context)
        )
        
        # Use ValueTracker for the moving point
        p1_prop = 0.5 # Center of curve
        p2_prop_tracker = ValueTracker(0.8)
        
        dot1 = Dot(curve_context.point_from_proportion(p1_prop), color=WHITE)
        dot2 = Dot(curve_context.point_from_proportion(p2_prop_tracker.get_value()), color=WHITE)
        
        # Secant line between the two dots
        secant = always_redraw(lambda: Line(
            dot1.get_center(), 
            dot2.get_center(), 
            color="#FFFF00", 
            stroke_width=2
        ) if np.linalg.norm(dot1.get_center() - dot2.get_center()) > 0.01 else Vector(direction=RIGHT, color="#FFFF00").move_to(dot1.get_center()).set_length(0.01))
        # Note: Vector is a fallback to avoid zero-length line issues if necessary, 
        # but Line(a, a) is usually okay or just invisible.
        
        self.play(Create(dot1), Create(dot2), Create(secant))
        
        # Move dot2 to dot1
        dot2.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(curve_context.point_from_proportion(p2_prop_tracker.get_value())))
        
        self.play(p2_prop_tracker.animate.set_value(p1_prop), run_time=3)
        dot2.clear_updaters()
        self.play(FadeOut(secant))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        diff_text = Text("Differentiation", font_size=32, color="#FF8C00")
        self.place_at_grid(diff_text, "F3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(diff_text))
        self.play(Flash(diff_text, color="#FF8C00"))
        self.wait(2)

    def construct(self):
        # Fetching title and lines from storyboard
        title = "Integration: Summing the Infinite"
        lines = [
            "Integration glues tiny, infinite pieces back into a whole.",
            "It calculates the total accumulation over a period.",
            "Visually, this is the area under a curve.",
            "If we sum every tiny drip from a bucket...",
            "We find the total volume of water lost."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_CURVE = "#00FFFF"
        COLOR_RECTS = "#FFFF00"
        COLOR_SWEEP = "#FF00FF"
        COLOR_AREA = "#FF8C00"
        COLOR_BUCKET = "#00FF00"
        COLOR_WATER = "#00FFFF"
        LECTURE_ACTIVE = "#FFFF00"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show a curve (#00FFFF) representing a leak rate. Divide the area under it into wide rectangles (#FFFF00).
        self.lecture[0].set_color(LECTURE_ACTIVE)
        
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4.2, 1],
            y_range=[0, 4.2, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=3,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False}
        ).scale(0.8)
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "E5")
        
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.15 * x**2 + 0.5, x_range=[0, 4], color=COLOR_CURVE)
        rects = axes.get_riemann_rectangles(curve, x_range=[0, 4], dx=0.8, color=COLOR_RECTS, fill_opacity=0.5)
        
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve))
        self.play(Create(rects))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Sweep a vertical line (#FF00FF) across the x-axis, filling the area under the curve.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(LECTURE_ACTIVE)
        
        tracker = ValueTracker(0.001)
        # Using a dummy area that will be updated
        sweep_area = axes.get_area(curve, x_range=[0, 0.001], color=COLOR_AREA, fill_opacity=0.5)
        sweep_line = Line(
            axes.c2p(0, 0), axes.c2p(0, curve.underlying_function(0)), 
            color=COLOR_SWEEP, stroke_width=4
        )
        
        def update_area(m):
            x_val = tracker.get_value()
            if x_val > 0.001:
                new_area = axes.get_area(curve, x_range=[0, x_val], color=COLOR_AREA, fill_opacity=0.5)
                m.become(new_area)
            
        def update_line(m):
            x_val = tracker.get_value()
            m.set_points_as_corners([
                axes.c2p(x_val, 0),
                axes.c2p(x_val, curve.underlying_function(x_val))
            ])

        self.play(FadeOut(rects))
        self.add(sweep_area, sweep_line)
        sweep_area.add_updater(update_area)
        sweep_line.add_updater(update_line)
        
        self.play(tracker.animate.set_value(4), run_time=3)
        sweep_area.remove_updater(update_area)
        sweep_line.remove_updater(update_line)
        self.play(FadeOut(sweep_line))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight the total filled area in #FF8C00. Label: 'Total Area'.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(LECTURE_ACTIVE)
        
        total_area_label = Text("Total Area", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(total_area_label, "B5")
        
        self.play(sweep_area.animate.set_fill(COLOR_AREA, opacity=0.8), Write(total_area_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Show a bucket icon (#00FF00) with drips falling into a pool (#00FFFF).
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(LECTURE_ACTIVE)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(axes), FadeOut(curve), FadeOut(sweep_area), FadeOut(total_area_label))
        
        bucket_points = [
            [-0.8, 1, 0], [-0.5, -1, 0], [0.5, -1, 0], [0.8, 1, 0]
        ]
        bucket = Polyline(*bucket_points, color=COLOR_BUCKET)
        self.place_in_area(bucket, "B3", "C4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        pool_rect = Rectangle(width=2, height=1, color=COLOR_WATER).set_stroke(COLOR_WATER, 2)
        self.place_in_area(pool_rect, "E3", "F4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Pool water
        pool_water = Rectangle(width=2, height=0.01, color=COLOR_WATER, fill_opacity=0.6, stroke_width=0)
        pool_water.move_to(pool_rect.get_bottom(), aligned_edge=DOWN)
        
        self.play(Create(bucket), Create(pool_rect), FadeIn(pool_water))
        
        drip_start = bucket.get_bottom() + UP*0.2
        drip_end = pool_rect.get_top() + DOWN*0.1
        
        for _ in range(4):
            drip = Dot(radius=0.06, color=COLOR_WATER).move_to(drip_start)
            self.play(drip.animate.move_to(drip_end), run_time=0.4, rate_func=linear)
            self.remove(drip)
            
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Show the water level in the pool rising to a 'Total Volume' mark.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(LECTURE_ACTIVE)
        
        water_height_tracker = ValueTracker(0.01)
        pool_water.add_updater(lambda m: m.stretch_to_fit_height(max(0.01, water_height_tracker.get_value()), about_edge=DOWN))
        
        vol_line = Line(pool_rect.get_left(), pool_rect.get_right(), color=WHITE).shift(UP*0.3)
        vol_label = Text("Total Volume", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        vol_label.next_to(vol_line, RIGHT, buff=0.1)

            water_height_tracker.animate.set_value(0.8),
            Create(vol_line),
            Write(vol_label),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

        water_height_tracker = ValueTracker(0.01)
        pool_water.add_updater(lambda m: m.stretch_to_fit_height(max(0.01, water_height_tracker.get_value()), about_edge=DOWN))
        
        vol_line = Line(pool_rect.get_left(), pool_rect.get_right(), color=WHITE).shift(UP*0.3)

outline.content: Reveal the 'Secret' of calculus: Differentiation and Integration are inverse operations. This is the bridge that connects the slope of a graph to the area underneath it. Use a 'Mountain Climber' visual to explain the link between height and steepness.
outline.example: A 'Growth Machine': If the machine tracks how fast a tree grows (Derivative), the total height of the tree (Integral) is simply the accumulation of that growth. One undoes the other.

        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

            for j, col in enumerate(cols):

                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

This section visualizes the connection between differentiation and integration using a dual-graph setup and intuitive metaphors (a mountain climber for steepness/height and a growing tree for rate/accumulation).

### Key Features:
- **Dual Representation**: The right side of the screen is split into four quadrants. The top quadrants show the mathematical relationship between a constant rate (Derivative) and a linear accumulation (Integral).
- **Visual Metaphors**:
  - **Mountain Climber**: Uses the requested `mountain.svg` asset to illustrate how local steepness (derivative) relates to total height.
  - **Growth Machine**: A growing tree demonstrates how tracking a growth rate results in a specific total height (accumulation).
- **The Great Bridge**: A final visual element connects the concepts of "Slope" and "Area," reinforcing the "Perfect Opposites" theme of the Fundamental Theorem.
- **Performance Optimized**: Replaced complex updaters and high-point-count plots with efficient transforms and standard Manim mobjects to ensure the section renders within the 180-second limit.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title_str = "The Fundamental Theorem: The Great Bridge"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Differentiation and integration are actually perfect opposites.",
            "One finds the slope, the other finds the area.",
            "A climber’s steepness at any point determines their height.",
            "Tracking growth rate reveals the total growth achieved.",
            "This bridge connects the rate of change to accumulation."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_str, lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Split screen: Left side shows a derivative graph, right shows an integral graph.
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # Derivative Graph: f(x) = 2 (Constant rate)
        deriv_axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4], y_range=[0, 4], x_length=2.5, y_length=2.0, 
                          axis_config={"include_tip": False, "color": BLUE_E})
        deriv_graph = deriv_axes.plot(lambda x: 2, x_range=[0, 3], color=YELLOW)
        deriv_label = Text("Derivative (Rate)", font_size=18, color=YELLOW)
        deriv_vg = VGroup(deriv_axes, deriv_graph, deriv_label).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        self.place_in_area(deriv_vg, "A1", "C3", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        # Integral Graph: F(x) = 2x (Accumulation)
        int_axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4], y_range=[0, 8], x_length=2.5, y_length=2.0, 
                        axis_config={"include_tip": False, "color": BLUE_E})
        int_graph = int_axes.plot(lambda x: 2*x, x_range=[0, 3], color=TEAL)
        int_label = Text("Integral (Total)", font_size=18, color=TEAL)
        int_vg = VGroup(int_axes, int_graph, int_label).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        self.place_in_area(int_vg, "A4", "C6", scale_factor=0.9)

        self.play(Create(deriv_vg), Create(int_vg), run_time=1.5)

        self.play(Create(slope_highlight), FadeIn(slope_label), FadeIn(area_highlight), FadeIn(area_label), run_time=1.0)
        self.wait(1)

        # Show a climber icon (#FF8C00) on a mountain [Asset: mountain.svg]; display steepness arrows.
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        mountain = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/mountain.svg").set_color(GREY)
        self.place_in_area(mountain, "D1", "F3", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        climber = Triangle(color="#FF8C00", fill_opacity=1).scale(0.12)
        climber.move_to(self.grid["E2"] + LEFT*0.2 + UP*0.3)
        
        steep_arrow = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=UP*0.5+RIGHT*0.5, color="#FF8C00").scale(0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(steep_arrow, "D1", scale_factor=1.0)
        steep_text = Text("Steepness", font_size=14, color="#FF8C00")
        self.place_at_grid(steep_text, "D1", scale_factor=1.0).next_to(steep_arrow, DOWN, buff=0.1)

        self.play(FadeIn(mountain), FadeIn(climber), GrowArrow(steep_arrow), Write(steep_text), run_time=1.0)

section_1.title: The Big Picture: Static vs. Dynamic
section_1.content: Introduction to the core philosophy of calculus. Contrast the world of algebra (static shapes and constant speeds) with the real world (curvy shapes and changing speeds). Use the 'Flash' vs. 'The Turtle' analogy to show the need for measuring change at a specific moment.
section_1.example: A car speeding up on a highway. Algebra tells you the average speed over an hour, but Calculus tells you the exact speed at the moment you pass a speed camera.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The Power of Approximation
section_2.content: Introduce the concept of 'Limits' and the 'Infinitesimal.' Explain how complex problems can be solved by breaking them into infinitely small, simpler pieces. This sets the stage for both derivatives and integrals.
section_2.example: Archimedes approximating a circle by fitting a polygon inside it. As the number of sides (n) approaches infinity, the polygon becomes the circle.

section_3.title: Differentiation: Zooming In for Truth
section_3.content: Focus on the 'Derivative.' Visually demonstrate that if you zoom in enough on any smooth curve, it eventually looks like a straight line. This 'straight line' is the tangent, representing the instantaneous rate of change.
section_3.example: A roller coaster track. At any single point on a steep drop, your 'direction' is a straight arrow (the derivative). We calculate this by making the distance between two points on the track infinitely small.

section_4.title: Integration: Summing the Infinite
section_4.content: Focus on the 'Integral.' Explain it as the reverse of slicing. If differentiation breaks things down, integration glues them back together to find the 'Total.' Represent this graphically as the area under a curve.
section_4.example: Calculating the total amount of water in a leaking bucket. If you know the 'rate' of the leak at every second (the derivative), integration sums those infinite tiny drips to tell you the total volume lost.

section_5.title: The Fundamental Theorem: The Great Bridge
section_5.content: Reveal the 'Secret' of calculus: Differentiation and Integration are inverse operations. This is the bridge that connects the slope of a graph to the area underneath it. Use a 'Mountain Climber' visual to explain the link between height and steepness.
section_5.example: A 'Growth Machine': If the machine tracks how fast a tree grows (Derivative), the total height of the tree (Integral) is simply the accumulation of that growth. One undoes the other.

section_6.title: Calculus in Action: The Modern World
section_6.content: Summarize how these two concepts allow us to model everything in motion. From planetary orbits to the spread of a virus, calculus is the 'engine' under the hood of physics and engineering.
section_6.example: A SpaceX Falcon 9 landing. Calculus is used to constantly calculate the changing fuel weight and air resistance to adjust the engines at every millisecond for a perfect touchdown.

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from shared state
        title = "Differentiation: Zooming In for Truth"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Zooming into any smooth curve eventually reveals a line.",
            "This straight line represents the instantaneous rate of change.",
            "On a roller coaster, your direction is a tangent.",
            "We find this by narrowing the gap between points.",
            "This process of finding slopes is called differentiation."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # Define a roller coaster curve (cubic for smooth look)
        curve_func = lambda x: 0.1 * x**3 - 0.2 * x
        curve = FunctionGraph(curve_func, x_range=[-3, 3], color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_in_area(curve, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Create(curve))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Zoom effect: Transition to a nearly straight line at x=0
        # Derivative at x=0: f'(0) = 0.3(0)^2 - 0.2 = -0.2
        # We simulate zoom by replacing with a straight segment
        line_start = self.grid["C2"]
        line_end = self.grid["E5"]
        zoomed_line = Line(start=line_start, end=line_end, color="#FFFF00")
        
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(curve, zoomed_line))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        tangent_label = Text("Tangent", font_size=24, color="#FF8C00")
        self.place_at_grid(tangent_label, "B3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(tangent_label))
        self.play(Flash(tangent_label, color="#FF8C00"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # Car icon - small triangle oriented along the line
        angle = np.arctan2(line_end[1] - line_start[1], line_end[0] - line_start[0])
        car = Triangle(color="#FFFF00", fill_opacity=1).scale(0.15)
        car.rotate(angle - PI/2) # Triangle default points UP
        car.move_to(line_start)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(car))
        self.play(car.animate.move_to(line_end), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # Transition back to curve to show points converging
        curve_context = FunctionGraph(curve_func, x_range=[-2.5, 2.5], color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_in_area(curve_context, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(zoomed_line, car, tangent_label),
            FadeIn(curve_context)
        )
        
        # Use ValueTracker for the moving point
        p1_prop = 0.5 # Center of curve
        p2_prop_tracker = ValueTracker(0.8)
        
        dot1 = Dot(curve_context.point_from_proportion(p1_prop), color=WHITE)
        dot2 = Dot(curve_context.point_from_proportion(p2_prop_tracker.get_value()), color=WHITE)
        
        # Secant line between the two dots
        secant = always_redraw(lambda: Line(
            dot1.get_center(), 
            dot2.get_center(), 
            color="#FFFF00", 
            stroke_width=2
        ) if np.linalg.norm(dot1.get_center() - dot2.get_center()) > 0.01 else Vector(direction=RIGHT, color="#FFFF00").move_to(dot1.get_center()).set_length(0.01))
        # Note: Vector is a fallback to avoid zero-length line issues if necessary, 
        # but Line(a, a) is usually okay or just invisible.
        
        self.play(Create(dot1), Create(dot2), Create(secant))
        
        # Move dot2 to dot1
        dot2.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(curve_context.point_from_proportion(p2_prop_tracker.get_value())))
        
        self.play(p2_prop_tracker.animate.set_value(p1_prop), run_time=3)
        dot2.clear_updaters()
        self.play(FadeOut(secant))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        diff_text = Text("Differentiation", font_size=32, color="#FF8C00")
        self.place_at_grid(diff_text, "F3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(diff_text))
        self.play(Flash(diff_text, color="#FF8C00"))
        self.wait(2)

    def construct(self):
        # Fetching title and lines from storyboard
        title = "Integration: Summing the Infinite"
        lines = [
            "Integration glues tiny, infinite pieces back into a whole.",
            "It calculates the total accumulation over a period.",
            "Visually, this is the area under a curve.",
            "If we sum every tiny drip from a bucket...",
            "We find the total volume of water lost."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_CURVE = "#00FFFF"
        COLOR_RECTS = "#FFFF00"
        COLOR_SWEEP = "#FF00FF"
        COLOR_AREA = "#FF8C00"
        COLOR_BUCKET = "#00FF00"
        COLOR_WATER = "#00FFFF"
        LECTURE_ACTIVE = "#FFFF00"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(LECTURE_ACTIVE)
        
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4.2, 1],
            y_range=[0, 4.2, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=3,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False}
        ).scale(0.8)
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "E5")
        
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.15 * x**2 + 0.5, x_range=[0, 4], color=COLOR_CURVE)
        rects = axes.get_riemann_rectangles(curve, x_range=[0, 4], dx=0.8, color=COLOR_RECTS, fill_opacity=0.5)
        
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve))
        self.play(Create(rects))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(LECTURE_ACTIVE)
        
        tracker = ValueTracker(0.001)
        sweep_area = axes.get_area(curve, x_range=[0, 0.001], color=COLOR_AREA, fill_opacity=0.5)
        sweep_line = Line(
            axes.c2p(0, 0), axes.c2p(0, curve.underlying_function(0)), 
            color=COLOR_SWEEP, stroke_width=4
        )
        
        def update_area(m):
            x_val = tracker.get_value()
            if x_val > 0.001:
                new_area = axes.get_area(curve, x_range=[0, x_val], color=COLOR_AREA, fill_opacity=0.5)
                m.become(new_area)
            
        def update_line(m):
            x_val = tracker.get_value()
            m.set_points_as_corners([
                axes.c2p(x_val, 0),
                axes.c2p(x_val, curve.underlying_function(x_val))
            ])

        self.play(FadeOut(rects))
        self.add(sweep_area, sweep_line)
        sweep_area.add_updater(update_area)
        sweep_line.add_updater(update_line)
        
        self.play(tracker.animate.set_value(4), run_time=3)
        sweep_area.remove_updater(update_area)
        sweep_line.remove_updater(update_line)
        self.play(FadeOut(sweep_line))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(LECTURE_ACTIVE)
        
        total_area_label = Text("Total Area", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(total_area_label, "B5")
        
        self.play(sweep_area.animate.set_fill(COLOR_AREA, opacity=0.8), Write(total_area_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(LECTURE_ACTIVE)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(axes), FadeOut(curve), FadeOut(sweep_area), FadeOut(total_area_label))
        
        bucket_points = [
            [-0.8, 1, 0], [-0.5, -1, 0], [0.5, -1, 0], [0.8, 1, 0]
        ]
        bucket = Polygon(*bucket_points, color=COLOR_BUCKET)
        self.place_in_area(bucket, "B3", "C4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        pool_rect = Rectangle(width=2, height=1, color=COLOR_WATER).set_stroke(COLOR_WATER, 2)
        self.place_in_area(pool_rect, "E3", "F4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Pool water
        pool_water = Rectangle(width=2, height=0.01, color=COLOR_WATER, fill_opacity=0.6, stroke_width=0)
        pool_water.move_to(pool_rect.get_bottom(), aligned_edge=DOWN)
        
        self.play(Create(bucket), Create(pool_rect), FadeIn(pool_water))
        
        drip_start = bucket.get_bottom() + UP*0.2
        drip_end = pool_rect.get_top() + DOWN*0.1
        
        for _ in range(4):
            drip = Dot(radius=0.06, color=COLOR_WATER).move_to(drip_start)
            self.play(drip.animate.move_to(drip_end), run_time=0.4, rate_func=linear)
            self.remove(drip)
            
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(LECTURE_ACTIVE)
        
        water_height_tracker = ValueTracker(0.01)
        pool_water.add_updater(lambda m: m.stretch_to_fit_height(max(0.01, water_height_tracker.get_value()), about_edge=DOWN))
        
        vol_line = Line(pool_rect.get_left(), pool_rect.get_right(), color=WHITE).shift(UP*0.3)
        vol_label = Text("Total Volume", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        vol_label.next_to(vol_line, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(
            water_height_tracker.animate.set_value(0.8),
            Create(vol_line),
            Write(vol_label),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

    def construct(self):

        lecture_lines = [
            "Differentiation and integration are actually perfect opposites.",
            "One finds the slope, the other finds the area.",
            "A climber’s steepness at any point determines their height.",
            "Tracking growth rate reveals the total growth achieved.",
            "This bridge connects the rate of change to accumulation."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_str, lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Split screen: Left side shows a derivative graph, right shows an integral graph.
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # Derivative Graph: f(x) = 2 (Constant rate)
        deriv_axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4], y_range=[0, 4], x_length=2.5, y_length=2.0, 
                          axis_config={"include_tip": False, "color": BLUE_E})
        deriv_graph = deriv_axes.plot(lambda x: 2, x_range=[0, 3], color=YELLOW)
        deriv_label = Text("Derivative (Rate)", font_size=18, color=YELLOW)
        deriv_vg = VGroup(deriv_axes, deriv_graph, deriv_label).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        self.place_in_area(deriv_vg, "A1", "C3", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        # Integral Graph: F(x) = 2x (Accumulation)
        int_axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4], y_range=[0, 8], x_length=2.5, y_length=2.0, 
                        axis_config={"include_tip": False, "color": BLUE_E})
        int_graph = int_axes.plot(lambda x: 2*x, x_range=[0, 3], color=TEAL)
        int_label = Text("Integral (Total)", font_size=18, color=TEAL)
        int_vg = VGroup(int_axes, int_graph, int_label).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        self.place_in_area(int_vg, "A4", "C6", scale_factor=0.9)

        self.play(Create(deriv_vg), Create(int_vg), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight the slope on the left (#FFFF00) and the area on the right (#00FFFF).
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # We'll highlight the 'Slope' concept on the derivative and 'Area' on the integral to show the link.
        slope_highlight = Line(deriv_axes.c2p(1, 2), deriv_axes.c2p(2, 2), color=YELLOW, stroke_width=8)
        slope_label = Text("Slope Value", font_size=16, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(slope_label, "C2", scale_factor=1.0)

        area_highlight = int_axes.get_area(int_graph, x_range=[0, 2], color="#00FFFF", opacity=0.4)
        area_label = Text("Area", font_size=16, color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(area_label, "C5", scale_factor=1.0)

        self.play(Create(slope_highlight), FadeIn(slope_label), FadeIn(area_highlight), FadeIn(area_label), run_time=1.0)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Show a climber icon (#FF8C00) on a mountain [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/mountain.svg]; display steepness arrows.
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        mountain = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/mountain.svg").set_color(GREY)
        self.place_in_area(mountain, "D1", "F3", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        climber = Triangle(color="#FF8C00", fill_opacity=1).scale(0.12)
        climber.move_to(self.grid["E2"] + LEFT*0.2 + UP*0.3)
        
        steep_arrow = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=UP*0.5+RIGHT*0.5, color="#FF8C00").scale(0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(steep_arrow, "D1", scale_factor=1.0)
        steep_text = Text("Steepness", font_size=14, color="#FF8C00")
        self.place_at_grid(steep_text, "D1", scale_factor=1.0).next_to(steep_arrow, DOWN, buff=0.1)

        self.play(FadeIn(mountain), FadeIn(climber), GrowArrow(steep_arrow), Write(steep_text), run_time=1.0)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Show a growing tree icon (#00FF00) whose height matches the integral area.
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        trunk = Rectangle(width=0.1, height=0.4, color="#8B4513", fill_opacity=1)
        foliage = Circle(radius=0.3, color="#00FF00", fill_opacity=0.8).move_to(trunk.get_top() + UP*0.2)
        tree = VGroup(trunk, foliage)
        self.place_in_area(tree, "D4", "F6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        tree_final = tree.copy()
        tree.scale(0.1, about_point=tree.get_bottom())
        
        growth_label = Text("Total Growth", font_size=16, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(growth_label, "F5", scale_factor=1.0)

        self.play(Transform(tree, tree_final), Write(growth_label), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Draw a bridge (#FFFFFF) connecting the concepts of 'Slope' and 'Area'.
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # Connect the Slope label (C2) and Area label (C5)
        bridge = Line(self.grid["C2"], self.grid["C5"], color=WHITE, stroke_width=6)
        bridge_label = Text("THE GREAT BRIDGE", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(bridge_label, "B2", "B5", scale_factor=1.0).shift(UP*0.5)

        self.play(Create(bridge), Write(bridge_label), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout with title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout("Calculus in Action: The Modern World", [
            "- Calculus is the engine powering modern physics and engineering.",
            "- It guides planets in orbit and rockets landing safely.",
            "- We use it to model anything that moves or changes."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show a rocket icon (#FFFF00) and an engine diagram (#00FFFF). Change lecture line 1 color to #FFFF00.
        
        # Rocket Icon
        rocket_body = Rectangle(width=0.3, height=0.6, fill_opacity=1, color="#FFFF00")
        rocket_tip = Triangle(fill_opacity=1, color="#FFFF00").scale(0.15).next_to(rocket_body, UP, buff=0)
        rocket_fin_l = Triangle(fill_opacity=1, color="#FFFF00").scale(0.1).rotate(PI/2).next_to(rocket_body, LEFT, buff=0).shift(DOWN*0.2)
        rocket_fin_r = Triangle(fill_opacity=1, color="#FFFF00").scale(0.1).rotate(-PI/2).next_to(rocket_body, RIGHT, buff=0).shift(DOWN*0.2)
        rocket = VGroup(rocket_body, rocket_tip, rocket_fin_l, rocket_fin_r)
        self.place_at_grid(rocket, "B2", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Engine Diagram (Simple abstract representation)
        engine_circle = Circle(radius=0.4, color="#00FFFF", stroke_width=2)
        engine_core = Dot(color="#00FFFF").scale(0.5)
        engine_rays = VGroup(*[Line(ORIGIN, 0.4*RIGHT, color="#00FFFF").rotate(a) for a in np.linspace(0, 2*PI, 12)])
        engine = VGroup(engine_circle, engine_core, engine_rays)
        self.place_at_grid(engine, "B5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"),
            FadeIn(rocket, shift=UP),
            Create(engine),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show planetary orbits (#00FF00) and the rocket landing sequence. Change lecture line 2 color to #FFFF00.
        
        # Orbits
        orbit_a = Ellipse(width=2.0, height=1.0, color="#00FF00").set_stroke(opacity=0.5)
        planet_a = Dot(color=WHITE, radius=0.08).move_to(orbit_a.point_at_angle(0))
        orbit_b = Ellipse(width=1.2, height=0.6, color="#00FF00").rotate(PI/3).set_stroke(opacity=0.5)
        planet_b = Dot(color=WHITE, radius=0.06).move_to(orbit_b.point_at_angle(PI/2))
        orbits_group = VGroup(orbit_a, planet_a, orbit_b, planet_b)
        self.place_in_area(orbits_group, "D1", "F3")
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"),
            Create(orbits_group),
            run_time=1
        )
        
        # Landing and Orbit animation
        self.play(
            MoveAlongPath(planet_a, orbit_a),
            MoveAlongPath(planet_b, orbit_b),
            rocket.animate.move_to(self.grid["F5"]).rotate(PI), # Descend and flip for landing
            run_time=4,
            rate_func=slow_into
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Flash icons for 'Weather', 'Stock Market', and 'Robotics' in #FF8C00. Change lecture line 3 color to #FFFF00.
        
        # Weather Icon
        weather_icon = VGroup(
            Circle(radius=0.15, color="#FF8C00", fill_opacity=1).shift(LEFT*0.1),
            Circle(radius=0.2, color="#FF8C00", fill_opacity=1).shift(UP*0.1),
            Circle(radius=0.15, color="#FF8C00", fill_opacity=1).shift(RIGHT*0.1)
        )
        self.place_at_grid(weather_icon, "C1", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Stock Market Icon
        stock_line = VMobject(color="#FF8C00", stroke_width=4)
        stock_line.set_points_as_corners([LEFT*0.3+DOWN*0.2, LEFT*0.1+UP*0.1, RIGHT*0.1+DOWN*0.1, RIGHT*0.3+UP*0.3])
        self.place_at_grid(stock_line, "C3", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Robotics Icon
        robotic_arm = VGroup(
            Line(ORIGIN, UP*0.3, color="#FF8C00", stroke_width=5),
            Line(UP*0.3, UP*0.3+RIGHT*0.3, color="#FF8C00", stroke_width=5),
            Dot(UP*0.3+RIGHT*0.3, color="#FF8C00")
        )
        self.place_at_grid(robotic_arm, "C5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        icons = VGroup(weather_icon, stock_line, robotic_arm)
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"),
            FadeIn(icons, scale=1.5),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(3)

outline.title: The Big Picture: Static vs. Dynamic
outline.content: Introduction to the core philosophy of calculus. Contrast the world of algebra (static shapes and constant speeds) with the real world (curvy shapes and changing speeds). Use the 'Flash' vs. 'The Turtle' analogy to show the need for measuring change at a specific moment.
outline.example: A car speeding up on a highway. Algebra tells you the average speed over an hour, but Calculus tells you the exact speed at the moment you pass a speed camera.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout with title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout("The Big Picture: Static vs. Dynamic", [
            "Algebra handles static shapes and constant speeds perfectly.",
            "But the real world is curvy and constantly changing.",
            "Calculus measures change at a specific, exact moment."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show a square (#00FF00) and a car icon (#FFFF00) moving at constant speed. 
        # Label: 'Algebra: Constant'. Change lecture line 1 color to #FFFF00.
        
        line1_color = "#FFFF00"
        square = Square(side_length=1.5, color="#00FF00", fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(square, "B3")
        
        # Simple car icon using a Triangle as requested by storyboard context
        car1 = Triangle(color="#FFFF00", fill_opacity=1).rotate(-PI/2).scale(0.2)
        car1.move_to(self.grid["C2"])
        
        label1 = Text("Algebra: Constant", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(label1, "A2")
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(line1_color),
            Create(square),
            FadeIn(car1),
            Write(label1)
        )
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Constant speed movement to grid C5
        self.play(car1.animate.move_to(self.grid["C5"]), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show a curve (#00FFFF) with a car icon (#FFFF00) accelerating. 
        # Label: 'Calculus: Changing'. Change lecture line 2 color to #FFFF00.
        
        # Create a quadratic curve for accelerating appearance
        curve = ParametricFunction(
            lambda t: np.array([t, 0.2 * t**2, 0]),
            t_range=[0, 3],
            color="#00FFFF"

        )

outline.title: Differentiation: Zooming In for Truth
outline.content: Focus on the 'Derivative.' Visually demonstrate that if you zoom in enough on any smooth curve, it eventually looks like a straight line. This 'straight line' is the tangent, representing the instantaneous rate of change.
outline.example: A roller coaster track. At any single point on a steep drop, your 'direction' is a straight arrow (the derivative). We calculate this by making the distance between two points on the track infinitely small.

outline.title: Integration: Summing the Infinite
outline.content: Focus on the 'Integral.' Explain it as the reverse of slicing. If differentiation breaks things down, integration glues them back together to find the 'Total.' Represent this graphically as the area under a curve.
outline.example: Calculating the total amount of water in a leaking bucket. If you know the 'rate' of the leak at every second (the derivative), integration sums those infinite tiny drips to tell you the total volume lost.

        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # Define a roller coaster curve (cubic for smooth look)
        curve_func = lambda x: 0.1 * x**3 - 0.2 * x
        curve = FunctionGraph(curve_func, x_range=[-3, 3], color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_in_area(curve, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Create(curve))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Zoom effect: Transition to a nearly straight line at x=0
        # Derivative at x=0: f'(0) = 0.3(0)^2 - 0.2 = -0.2

        line_start = self.grid["C2"]
        line_end = self.grid["E5"]
        zoomed_line = Line(start=line_start, end=line_end, color="#FFFF00")
        
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(curve, zoomed_line))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        tangent_label = Text("Tangent", font_size=24, color="#FF8C00")
        self.place_at_grid(tangent_label, "B3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(tangent_label))
        self.play(Flash(tangent_label, color="#FF8C00"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # Car icon - small triangle oriented along the line
        angle = np.arctan2(line_end[1] - line_start[1], line_end[0] - line_start[0])
        car = Triangle(color="#FFFF00", fill_opacity=1).scale(0.15)
        car.rotate(angle - PI/2) # Triangle default points UP
        car.move_to(line_start)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(car))
        self.play(car.animate.move_to(line_end), run_time=2, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # Transition back to curve to show points converging
        curve_context = FunctionGraph(curve_func, x_range=[-2.5, 2.5], color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_in_area(curve_context, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(zoomed_line, car, tangent_label),
            FadeIn(curve_context)
        )
        
        # Use ValueTracker for the moving point
        p1_prop = 0.5 # Center of curve
        p2_prop_tracker = ValueTracker(0.8)
        
        dot1 = Dot(curve_context.point_from_proportion(p1_prop), color=WHITE)
        dot2 = Dot(curve_context.point_from_proportion(p2_prop_tracker.get_value()), color=WHITE)
        
        # Secant line between the two dots
        secant = always_redraw(lambda: Line(
            dot1.get_center(), 
            dot2.get_center(), 
            color="#FFFF00", 
            stroke_width=2
        ) if np.linalg.norm(dot1.get_center() - dot2.get_center()) > 0.01 else Vector(direction=RIGHT, color="#FFFF00").move_to(dot1.get_center()).set_length(0.01))
        # Note: Vector is a fallback to avoid zero-length line issues if necessary, 
        # but Line(a, a) is usually okay or just invisible.
        
        self.play(Create(dot1), Create(dot2), Create(secant))
        
        # Move dot2 to dot1
        dot2.add_updater(lambda d: d.move_to(curve_context.point_from_proportion(p2_prop_tracker.get_value())))
        
        self.play(p2_prop_tracker.animate.set_value(p1_prop), run_time=3)
        dot2.clear_updaters()
        self.play(FadeOut(secant))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        diff_text = Text("Differentiation", font_size=32, color="#FF8C00")

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Fetching title and lines from storyboard
        title = "Integration: Summing the Infinite"
        lines = [
            "Integration glues tiny, infinite pieces back into a whole.",
            "It calculates the total accumulation over a period.",
            "Visually, this is the area under a curve.",
            "If we sum every tiny drip from a bucket...",
            "We find the total volume of water lost."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_CURVE = "#00FFFF"
        COLOR_RECTS = "#FFFF00"
        COLOR_SWEEP = "#FF00FF"
        COLOR_AREA = "#FF8C00"
        COLOR_BUCKET = "#00FF00"
        COLOR_WATER = "#00FFFF"
        LECTURE_ACTIVE = "#FFFF00"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(LECTURE_ACTIVE)
        
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4.2, 1],
            y_range=[0, 4.2, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=3,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False}
        ).scale(0.8)
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B2", "E5")
        
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.15 * x**2 + 0.5, x_range=[0, 4], color=COLOR_CURVE)
        rects = axes.get_riemann_rectangles(curve, x_range=[0, 4], dx=0.8, color=COLOR_RECTS, fill_opacity=0.5)
        
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(curve))
        self.play(Create(rects))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(LECTURE_ACTIVE)
        
        tracker = ValueTracker(0.001)
        sweep_area = axes.get_area(curve, x_range=[0, 0.001], color=COLOR_AREA, fill_opacity=0.5)
        sweep_line = Line(
            axes.c2p(0, 0), axes.c2p(0, curve.underlying_function(0)), 
            color=COLOR_SWEEP, stroke_width=4
        )
        
        def update_area(m):
            x_val = tracker.get_value()
            if x_val > 0.001:
                new_area = axes.get_area(curve, x_range=[0, x_val], color=COLOR_AREA, fill_opacity=0.5)
                m.become(new_area)
            
        def update_line(m):
            x_val = tracker.get_value()
            m.set_points_as_corners([
                axes.c2p(x_val, 0),
                axes.c2p(x_val, curve.underlying_function(x_val))
            ])

        self.play(FadeOut(rects))
        self.add(sweep_area, sweep_line)
        sweep_area.add_updater(update_area)
        sweep_line.add_updater(update_line)
        
        self.play(tracker.animate.set_value(4), run_time=3)
        sweep_area.remove_updater(update_area)
        sweep_line.remove_updater(update_line)
        self.play(FadeOut(sweep_line))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(LECTURE_ACTIVE)
        
        total_area_label = Text("Total Area", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(total_area_label, "B5")
        
        self.play(sweep_area.animate.set_fill(COLOR_AREA, opacity=0.8), Write(total_area_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(LECTURE_ACTIVE)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(axes), FadeOut(curve), FadeOut(sweep_area), FadeOut(total_area_label))
        
        bucket_points = [
            [-0.8, 1, 0], [-0.5, -1, 0], [0.5, -1, 0], [0.8, 1, 0]
        ]
        bucket = Polygon(*bucket_points, color=COLOR_BUCKET)
        self.place_in_area(bucket, "B3", "C4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        pool_rect = Rectangle(width=2, height=1, color=COLOR_WATER).set_stroke(COLOR_WATER, 2)
        self.place_in_area(pool_rect, "E3", "F4", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Pool water
        pool_water = Rectangle(width=2, height=0.01, color=COLOR_WATER, fill_opacity=0.6, stroke_width=0)
        pool_water.move_to(pool_rect.get_bottom(), aligned_edge=DOWN)
        
        self.play(Create(bucket), Create(pool_rect), FadeIn(pool_water))
        
        drip_start = bucket.get_bottom() + UP*0.2
        drip_end = pool_rect.get_top() + DOWN*0.1
        
        for _ in range(4):
            drip = Dot(radius=0.06, color=COLOR_WATER).move_to(drip_start)
            self.play(drip.animate.move_to(drip_end), run_time=0.4, rate_func=linear)
            self.remove(drip)
            
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(LECTURE_ACTIVE)
        
        water_height_tracker = ValueTracker(0.01)
        pool_water.add_updater(lambda m: m.stretch_to_fit_height(max(0.01, water_height_tracker.get_value()), about_edge=DOWN))
        
        vol_line = Line(pool_rect.get_left(), pool_rect.get_right(), color=WHITE).shift(UP*0.3)
        vol_label = Text("Total Volume", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        vol_label.next_to(vol_line, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(
            water_height_tracker.animate.set_value(0.8),
            Create(vol_line),
            Write(vol_label),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

outline.title: The Fundamental Theorem: The Great Bridge
outline.content: Reveal the 'Secret' of calculus: Differentiation and Integration are inverse operations. This is the bridge that connects the slope of a graph to the area underneath it. Use a 'Mountain Climber' visual to explain the link between height and steepness.
outline.example: A 'Growth Machine': If the machine tracks how fast a tree grows (Derivative), the total height of the tree (Integral) is simply the accumulation of that growth. One undoes the other.

storyboard.title: The Fundamental Theorem: The Great Bridge
lecture_lines: Differentiation and integration are actually perfect opposites.
One finds the slope, the other finds the area.
A climber’s steepness at any point determines their height.
Tracking growth rate reveals the total growth achieved.
This bridge connects the rate of change to accumulation.

Show a growing tree icon (#00FF00) whose height matches the integral area. Change lecture line 4 color to #FFFF00.
Draw a bridge (#FFFFFF) connecting the concepts of 'Slope' and 'Area'. Change lecture line 5 color to #FFFF00.

        # Integral Graph: F(x) = 2x (Accumulation)

                        axis_config={"include_tip": False, "color": BLUE_E})
        int_graph = int_axes.plot(lambda x: 2*x, x_range=[0, 3], color=TEAL)
        int_label = Text("Integral (Total)", font_size=18, color=TEAL)

        self.place_in_area(int_vg, "A4", "C6", scale_factor=0.9)

outline.content: Summarize how these two concepts allow us to model everything in motion. From planetary orbits to the spread of a virus, calculus is the 'engine' under the hood of physics and engineering.
outline.example: A SpaceX Falcon 9 landing. Calculus is used to constantly calculate the changing fuel weight and air resistance to adjust the engines at every millisecond for a perfect touchdown.
